undeclare-the-file-that-prints-it.why: Proves the gate detects a REAL occurrence of the real literal in a real tracked document, rather than only the synthetic ones in its self-test. With the declaration removed, docs/phase-2-walkthrough.md -- which holds it four times -- must be named. ⛔ THE OBVIOUS PLANT IS NOT AVAILABLE AND THAT IS THE POINT: writing the password into docs/first-run.md would require putting the literal into this tracked plant file, which is the exact defect the gate exists to stop. So the budget-zero direction on the subject itself is proven by the self-test case `the guide prints the seeded password`, on a synthetic tree with a synthetic secret, and the real-tree plant proves the detection on the real one.

blind-the-derivation.why: Proves the NON-VACUITY FLOOR. With no seed script in scope the derivation finds zero passwords, every count loop runs over an empty set, and a gate without this floor would print a confident green over its own subject -- which this repository has already shipped once, in check:process-prefix, which reported ZERO with the defect planted in front of it. EXPECTED_SECRET_COUNT must make it fail with `must not report green` instead.
